assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT is the organizing framework for strongly correlated electrons: the exact infinite-dimension limit and the mapping onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem gave the first non-perturbative handle on the Mott transition, and combined with density functional theory (DFT+DMFT) it lets one compute spectra and phase behaviour of real transition-metal, f-electron and oxide materials. It is original, conceptually clear and has had a three-decade effect on how correlated materials are modelled, which is the part of the field I know best.
assessment.attribution: The infinite-dimension limit is usually credited to Metzner and Vollhardt (1989), the impurity mapping and self-consistency to Georges and Kotliar (1992), with important contributions from Jarrell, Rozenberg and others. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt are the supplied names that best span the conceptual steps, but the credit chain is not clean and a tidy three-person split omits people outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: widely reproduced, embedded in codes and used in quantitative comparison with photoemission, optics and neutron data. Recognition is well within the expected timescale and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Metzner is not among the credited names, so the foundational step of the infinite-dimension limit may be under-attributed.
Quantitative predictive power of DFT+DMFT depends on double-counting and interaction-parameter choices, so the fully first-principles claim is partly contested.
Whether the committee views this as a method or as a discovery is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of moire flat bands at the magic angle (Bistritzer-MacDonald) followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable, clean platform for strongly correlated and topological physics that is not available in conventional materials. It is original, clear and has spawned a large subfield (moire materials, fractional Chern insulators, twistronics) on which my field's electronic-structure methods are being heavily tested.
assessment.attribution: Prediction of the magic angle is clearly Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011); the experimental discovery is associated with Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (2018), where the first author of the key papers is a junior researcher not in the supplied credit. A theory-plus-experiment configuration is natural, but the list excludes some decisive experimentalists and other twist-angle theorists.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups across several materials, with the principal phases reproduced. The field is still evolving and the origin of the superconductivity is not settled, but the discovery itself is secure and recognition is plausibly timely.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated.
Sample-dependent behaviour and twist-angle disorder complicate the universality of results.
Credit for the experimental discovery extends beyond the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the large effect in crystalline MgO barriers, gave the read heads of hard disks and the basis of MRAM. It combines a physics insight (spin-dependent tunnelling and coherent symmetry filtering of Bloch states, which first-principles calculations explained) with enormous technological reach. It is the natural successor to the GMR prize in the magnetism domain.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin (and Yuasa and collaborators in Japan) realised the giant MgO effect in 2004, with Butler and Mathon-Umerski providing the theory. The supplied three names cover the core experimental line, but Yuasa and the theorists are excluded, so the allocation is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: more than two decades of commercial deployment and independent confirmation. It has arguably waited long enough that timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier GMR prize may reduce perceived novelty.
Credit among Parkin, Yuasa and the Japanese groups for MgO is contested and the list omits Yuasa.
The invention aspect may outweigh pure discovery content.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and confirmed the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism for which theory was already recognised. The detectors, trigger and analysis machinery are monumental, and the physical result is clear and lasting. This is outside my own field, so I weigh it by the general standard of importance and confirmation.
assessment.attribution: The experimental discovery belongs to the ATLAS and CMS collaborations of thousands. The proposed spokesperson-and-founder trio is a conventional but imperfect proxy and the list cannot resolve who made the decisive contributions among accelerator, detector and analysis leaders.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and subsequently measured in many channels; the interpretation is stable. Timeliness is high given more than a decade since discovery.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit does not fit the three-person limit cleanly.
Choice among the founders and spokespersons is partly subjective.
I am relying on general knowledge outside my area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new class of electronic phases defined by band topology and spin-orbit coupling, with robust boundary states. It linked first-principles band structure to topology and has strongly shaped materials discovery. Originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed edge transport in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied names omit Bernevig, Zhang, Hughes and the 3D topological insulator groups, so the configuration is incomplete in credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive independent ARPES and transport confirmation in 3D materials, though the HgTe quantum spin Hall conductance is less quantitatively clean. Partly overlapped by the 2016 topology prize, which reduces headroom.
uncertainties: The 2016 prize on topological phases may make a second topological award less likely.
Important proposers (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and 3D experimenters are outside the credited names.
Quantisation in the edge channels is less precise than in the quantum Hall case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability, redefine the limit of time and frequency measurement and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is original, clear and has high practical and scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye achieved the leading clock performance; two laureates are a clean configuration, with other contributors (Hollberg, Lemonde, Takamoto) in a secondary position.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many laboratories at the 1e-18 level. The redefinition of the SI second is still pending, so recognition is somewhat early on practical impact but sound on science.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes may reduce novelty.
Contributions by other groups complicate sharp attribution.
The redefinition of the second has not yet happened.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental realisation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators shows a quantised Hall resistance without an external field, which intersects magnetism and topology directly. It is a clear, elegant discovery and has potential for low-dissipation electronics, and it combines theory predictions with materials engineering.
assessment.attribution: Dai and Fang and collaborators predicted the effect in Cr- or Fe-doped Bi2Te3 materials, and Xue's group observed it in 2013; others (Chang, Wang, Moodera) also contributed. The supplied trio is plausible, but the experimental credit is shared across groups and the prediction involves a larger team.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed, though the quantisation temperature remains very low, which limits applications; the field is still maturing, and timing is somewhat early but not premature.
uncertainties: Operating temperature remains below about 1 K in the cleanest samples, so practical impact is uncertain.
Credit among theory and multiple experimental groups is unresolved.
The topology prize in 2016 reduces headroom.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-model physics, the superfluid-Mott transition and single-site resolved many-body states in a controlled setting, bridging condensed-matter theory and atomic physics. It is clear and has had lasting impact, although it follows the Bose-Einstein condensation prize.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and collaborators proposed the Hubbard-model realisation, Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition and developed microscopy, and Esslinger demonstrated fermionic Mott states. Selecting three of four credited names leaves a notable person out and the split is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many groups. Quantitative cooling to the antiferromagnetic regime remains challenging, so the long-term promise of solving open problems in correlated materials is not yet delivered.
uncertainties: Whether simulators have solved a problem beyond classical computation is unresolved.
Four credited names for a three-person limit makes allocation arbitrary.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes.
